notes.meaning: The Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were only two days away. The chief priests and teachers of the law were looking for a secret, sneaky way to arrest Jesus and put Him to death. They wanted to destroy Him, but they knew they had to hide their plans from the crowds.

The religious leaders decided not to arrest Jesus during the festival days. Huge crowds of pilgrims filled Jerusalem for the feast, and many people viewed Jesus as a prophet. The leaders were terrified that taking Him openly would cause a violent riot among the people.

While Jesus was eating dinner in Bethany at the house of Simon the Leper, a woman came in with an alabaster jar filled with pure, costly nard perfume. She broke the jar open and poured the fragrant oil over Jesus' head. Her action was a bold, loving gift of deep honor toward Him.

Some of the people sitting at the table became very upset when they saw what she did. They began complaining to each other that such expensive perfume was being wasted. They could not understand pouring out something so valuable in a single moment.

They pointed out that the perfume was worth more than three hundred silver coins, which was a full year of wages for a working person. That money could have been given to help the poor, which was an important duty during Passover. Instead of seeing her love, they scolded her harshly.

Jesus immediately stepped in to defend the woman and told the guests to leave her alone. He asked why they were bothering her when she had just done a beautiful and noble deed for Him. What seemed like a waste to others was deeply precious to the Lord.

Jesus reminded His disciples that poor people would always be around, and they could help them at any time. But Jesus Himself would only be with them in bodily form for a very short time. His earthly life was almost over, making this a unique moment to honor Him directly.

Jesus explained that the woman had done all she had the power to do. Even if she did not fully understand what was coming, she had anointed His body ahead of time for His burial. God used her loving gift to prepare Jesus for the grave before His death arrived.

Jesus promised that wherever the good news of salvation is preached across the world, what this woman did would be told in memory of her. Human monuments crumble, but her faithful act of love would never be forgotten. Her story still teaches believers to give their best to Christ.

Judas Iscariot, one of Jesus' twelve chosen disciples, left the group and went to the chief priests. He offered to hand Jesus over into their control. His hurt feelings and greed drove him to turn against his own Master.

The chief priests were thrilled by Judas' offer because having an insider help them made their plot much easier. They promised to pay him money for his help. From that moment on, Judas searched for an opportunity to betray Jesus away from the crowds.

On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Passover lambs were sacrificed at the temple. The disciples asked Jesus where He wanted them to go and get the Passover meal ready for Him. Even while facing death, Jesus was careful to obey God's law.

Jesus sent two of His disciples into Jerusalem with very specific instructions. He told them they would meet a man carrying a water jug, and they should simply follow him. Jesus showed His complete foreknowledge by predicting exactly what they would see.

Jesus told the disciples to speak to the owner of whatever house the man entered. They were to ask where the guest room was so the Teacher could eat the Passover with His disciples. Jesus spoke with quiet authority as the Master who had need of the room.

Jesus said the owner would show them a large upstairs room that was already swept, set with couches, and ready. The disciples were told to prepare the Passover meal there. Jesus arranged this private room so He could spend His last evening alone with His disciples.

The two disciples went into the city and found everything just as Jesus had said it would be. They followed His directions and prepared the Passover meal, including the roasted lamb and unleavened bread. Seeing His words come true strengthened their trust in Him.

When evening arrived, Jesus came to the upper room with the Twelve. The disciples who had prepared the meal were joined by Jesus and the rest of the group. Together, they gathered to share the solemn holy day meal.

While they were reclining at the table eating, Jesus made a startling announcement. He told them that one of the men eating with Him would betray Him. In Jewish culture, sharing a meal was a pledge of friendship, which made this betrayal especially heartbreaking.

The disciples were filled with deep sorrow and confusion when they heard Jesus speak of betrayal. One after another, they began asking Him if they were the guilty person. They searched their own hearts, horrified that one of their close group could do such a thing.

Jesus answered that the traitor was one of the Twelve who was dipping food into the shared bowl with Him. This showed how close the betrayer was to Jesus and made his disloyalty all the more wicked. Even so, Jesus did not call Judas out by name to the rest of the group.

Jesus explained that the Son of Man must die just as the Old Testament Scriptures had foretold. Even though His death was part of God's sovereign plan, the man who betrayed Him was still fully guilty of his terrible sin. Jesus warned that it would have been better for that man never to have been born.

During the meal, Jesus took bread, blessed God for providing food, broke it into pieces, and gave it to His disciples. He told them to take it, saying that this was His body. In this moment, Jesus started the Lord's Supper, pointing forward to how His body would soon be broken on the cross for them.

differ.view: Christ's true physical body is genuinely present in, with, and under the bread.
The bread remains bread, but believers spiritually feed on Christ's true body by faith.
The bread is a symbolic sign that points to Christ's body as a memorial.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The bread is transformed into the actual body of Jesus Christ, while only the appearance of bread remains.

notes.meaning: Next, Jesus took the cup of wine, gave thanks to God, and handed it to His disciples. Every one of them drank from it together. This shared cup united them in the new memorial meal He was establishing.

Jesus told them that this was His blood of the covenant, which was poured out for many people. A covenant is a sacred agreement between God and His people, and Jesus' blood sealed this new relationship. His death was a willing sacrifice that would bring forgiveness and salvation to the world.
